sections.title: One more verb, one more case ending
sections.content: *visszatekint* ("to look back") almost always needs a sublative object — the thing you're looking back at takes -ra/-re, not accusative -t. *Ha visszatekintek* + noun-ra/-re gives you a ready-made frame for starting a reflection: *Ha visszatekintek az elmúlt évekre, azt látom, hogy...* ("Looking back at the past years, I see that...").

items.spanish: Ha visszatekintek az elmúlt évekre, sokat változtam.
items.english: Looking back at the past years, I've changed a lot.
Looking back, I consider it a mature decision.
It's strange to look back at that day.

sections.content: *visszatekintve* on its own, without any object, works as a floating opener for a whole sentence — *Visszatekintve, minden más volt* ("Looking back, everything was different") — while *visszatekintek valamire* needs that -ra/-re noun to say exactly what you're looking back at.
